title: Containment and follow-up for scheduler probe that caused unfused-kernel flapping under mixed-quant load
creator: Asha Khatri
description: On 2026-02-19 22:10 UTC a scheduler change that increased probe frequency for path selection caused large p95/p99 latency spikes for a subset of production traffic using mixed-quant models (mostly 8-bit + 4-bit layers). The scheduler started favoring an unfused attention kernel for certain sequence-length and batch-size combinations; the unfused kernel performs worse at small micro-batch sizes but had been selected based on stale microbenchmark weights. This ticket captures immediate containment steps, a technical mitigation plan, follow-ups to prevent regression recurrence, and monitoring/alert requirements.
timeline_summary: 2026-02-19 22:05 UTC: rolling restart pushed scheduler change that increases probe window from 120s to 300s for faster adaptation (release runtime-1.23.0)
2026-02-19 22:10 UTC: customer SLO alerts trigger — rapid p95 increase observed on several dedicated pools serving mixed-quant models
2026-02-19 22:17 UTC: on-call identifies higher rate of unfused-kernel assignments in runtime traces and opens incident
2026-02-19 22:40 UTC: emergency rollback of scheduler probe frequency to previous value; p95 returns to baseline within two minutes
2026-02-19 23:05 UTC: temporary circuit breaker deployed to limit kernel probing for pools with high mixed-quant ratio
2026-02-20 09:00 UTC: incident declared stable; root-cause investigation begins
root_cause: Scheduler probe frequency increase caused more frequent kernel microbench re-evaluation under production noise
Kernel selector used aggregated microbenchmark weights gathered from isolated perf runs that did not reflect mixed-quant execution characteristics at small micro-batch sizes
Autotile threshold heuristic misclassified sequences of lengths 128-256 in presence of KV-cache hits leading to unfused kernel preference
No canary coverage for dedicated pools running mixed-quant models and no alerting on sudden kernel-assignment distribution shifts
mitigations_taken: Rolled back probe frequency to previous stable value (runtime-1.23.1 rollback) — immediate customer impact mitigated
Deployed temporary circuit breaker: limit probe retries to 1 per 30 minutes for pools with >30% mixed-quant requests
Added ad-hoc dashboard showing kernel-assignment distribution per pool and p95 correlation
Notified top impacted customers and opened support tickets where SLAs were at risk
postmortem_action_items: A1: Implement weighted kernel selector that incorporates production microbenchmarks for mixed-quant and small micro-batch scenarios — owner: Marco Lebedev — due: 2026-03-24
A2: Add an automated canary that runs mixed-quant workloads in dedicated pools before scheduler heuristic changes are promoted — owner: Linh Tran — due: 2026-04-07
A3: Create an alert on kernel-assignment distribution divergence (KL > 0.15 relative to baseline) and p95 covariance > 2x for any pool — owner: SRE Team (owner: Priya Menon) — due: 2026-03-17

A4: Extend regression test harness with synthetic mixed-quant traces and per-kernel microbench marking; run in CI on every scheduler and kernel selector PR — owner: Bench Team (owner: Diego Alvarez) — due: 2026-03-31
A5: Hard guard in scheduler: when probing, require a minimum population of micro-batches (N>=16) before switching to an unfused kernel — owner: Marco Lebedev — due: 2026-03-20
A6: Add telemetry to mark micro-batch-size, seq-len, kv-cache-hit-rate alongside kernel choice for long-term analysis — owner: Telemetry Team (owner: Noor Rahman) — due: 2026-03-10 (in progress)
A7: Post-incident review session and runbook update to include steps to rollback probe changes and apply circuit breakers — owner: Asha Khatri — due: 2026-03-12
risks_and_tradeoffs: Slowing probe frequency reduces adaptability to workload shifts and may postpone beneficial kernel migrations
Weighted kernel selection increases reliance on production microbench data which must be carefully guarded to avoid noise and feedback loops
Canary coverage for dedicated pools increases rollout latency and requires additional infra cost for synthetic traffic
testing_and_validation_plan: Introduce deterministic replay of archived production traces into a staging fleet that mirrors dedicated pools
Benchmark unfused vs fused attention kernels across a matrix of seq-len, micro-batch, and kv-cache hit-rate with mixed-quant models; publish to the model-catalog perf table
Run scheduled nightly chaos tests that briefly perturb probe thresholds and verify circuit breaker kicks in and rollbacks are automated
